insight: Terrain inversion: color 5 (with color-3 decorative dots) is NOT-walkable (wall). Color 10 (`a`) IS walkable. The sprite temporarily renders `5` under itself while traversing an `a` cell, reverting on departure. Total `a` count is conserved by pure motion.

ACTION7 = full-state UNDO of the last modifying action (pops the undo stack). Confirmed: after clicking an item then ACTION7 two turns later, the item was RESTORED (color-14 count went from 0 back to 21). UNDO still costs 1 turn. It's not just player-position undo — it reverts item destruction too. Useful when you want to try a click/move and back it out, but it doesn't expand your budget.

ACTION3 = move LEFT one 5-cell step. ACTION4 = move RIGHT one 5-cell step. Step is discrete: if the adjacent step-destination is wall (color 5), the action is blocked and only the turn-counter advances. Player only moves horizontally — no vertical motion action exists in [3,4,6,7]. To reach upper rows the player must either wait for them to become connected via item-destruction-created corridors + some missing mechanic I haven't found, or the game has a different primary loop that isn't "navigate".

Destroying a middle-cluster `e` item (rows 13-17, cols 31-35 / 37-41 / 43-47 / 49-53) ALSO converts the adjacent row-12 and row-18 wall cells above/below the item's 5-col footprint into walkable `a`, creating a VERTICAL TUNNEL through those wall belts. Destroying top-cluster items (rows 1-5) just opens the item footprint but does not cut through rows 6-11. The walls at rows 6-11 appear to stay as `5` regardless.

Destroying ALL 7 items on L1 does NOT auto-win. State stays NOT_FINISHED. So the win condition is not 'clear all items'. Most likely: after opening the walkable corridor via items, something else (the player reaching a target, or a specific item-click order) triggers the win. Player at col 43-47 under the vertical tunnel is a candidate — but reaching it costs ~5-6 ACTION4 steps, so the solve almost certainly can't use all 7 clicks AND also walk there within 15 turns.

Click on empty `a` cell (no item there) is a no-op: only the turn counter advances, player doesn't move, nothing else changes. So ACTION6 is NOT a teleport/move-to mechanic — it's strictly item-destruction targeted at color-14 items. Click on wall (`5`) untested but probably also a no-op. Implication: the player's only positional control is ACTION3/4 (±5 cells horizontal). Vertical motion must come from something we haven't unlocked yet — maybe an ACTION we haven't tried on a specific state, or gravity that activates only in specific conditions.
